= Glasgow Kinship Circle — Evidence Register =

<small>'''Glasgow Name Study:''' [[Space:Glasgow Name Study|project home]] · [[Space:Glasgow Research|research directory]] · [[Space:Repeated Glasgow Marriages|marriage dataset]] · [[Space:Glasgow Branches in 15th and 16th Century Scotland|early Scottish branches]] · [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/compare compare people]</small>

This page holds the detailed relationship and association evidence around Glasgow-surname people. The sixteenth-century burgh records support a probable immediate family around William Glasgow and Esbell Brade; later repeated Stewart–Cunningham–Glasgow connections remain separate working hypotheses to test across Scotland, Ulster and America.

== Current early-burgh reconstruction ==

{| class="wikitable" style="background:#eaf7df; width:100%;"
|-
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | What the combined property, craft and in-law evidence supports
|-
| ✅ [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]] and [[Brade-232|Esbell Brade]] expressly transferred property to '''their son [[Glasgow-1093|John]]''' in 1534, and John received sasine as William's heir in 1564.<br/><br/>🟡 [[Glasgow-1096|Robert]] and [[Glasgow-1097|Archibald]] were probably William's sons and John's brothers; [[Glasgow-3916|Isobella]] was probably William's daughter and John's sister. Their recurring adjoining property, fishing craft, witnessing and in-law links agree across several independent transactions. No surviving act states those three kin terms, so the profile edges must remain uncertain and a close-collateral reconstruction remains possible.<br/><br/>⚠️ [[Glasgow-3915|Elizabeth Glasgow]], wife of Alexander Kaine, is only a possible daughter or close kinswoman. Her evidence is an associate-and-estate link, not a title succession or stated relationship.
|}

== Profile-linked marriage leads ==

The following links preserve the working dataset while avoiding unsupported claims about strategy, nobility, property or migration. Each pair needs its own record-level assessment.

* [[Cunningham-20923|Jonet Cunningham]] and [[Glasgow-1027|Robert Glasgow]] — profile-linked couple; the reported 1613 parish entry requires direct inspection.
* [[Cunningham-20926|Agnes Cunningham]] and [[Glasgow-1321|Alexander Glasgow]] — profile-linked couple; their son's baptism is presently stronger evidence than a marriage record.
* [[Cunningham-20927|Jean Cunningham]] and [[Glasgow-1483|James Glasgow]] — profile-linked Govan couple; do not mistake James's approximate 1790 birth year for a marriage date.
* [[Glasgow-543|Nancy Glasgow]] and [[Cunningham-13540|Abraham Cunningham]] — later profile-linked couple; independent evidence does not connect this Abraham to the earlier Cunningham spouses.
* [[Stewart-65226|Margaret Stewart]], [[Glasgow-3061|Jonet Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1100|Margarat Glasgow]] — separate Stewart marriage leads; a shared spouse surname does not prove one Stewart branch or royal descent.
* [[Glasgow-3613|Margaret Smith]], [[Meik-14|Jonet Meik]], [[Hamilton-31734|Catherine Hamilton]] and [[Wilson-127012|Thomas Wilson]] — early spouse-profile leads retained for record checking, not evidence of one coordinated kin group.

== What the surname counts show ==

The [[Space:Repeated Glasgow Marriages|Repeated Glasgow Marriages]] page counts spouse surnames in two working profile sets. That is useful for prioritising searches and detecting possible duplicate families. It does '''not''' establish:

* that two spouses with the same surname were related;
* that a marriage was arranged for political or economic advantage;
* descent from a noble, chiefly or royal house;
* ownership of connected land;
* a shared Presbyterian, mercantile or migration network; or
* a continuous Scotland-to-Ulster-to-America lineage.

Common surnames such as Smith, Wilson, Anderson, Robertson and Stewart require especially careful separation by parish, occupation, relatives and witnesses.

== Working hypotheses ==

The repeated marriages and property associations may reflect a “three-stranded” Glasgow–Stewart–Cunningham network, and migration routes may have followed kin or familiar community connections. Those ideas are retained here as research hypotheses. The next step is to look for the records that could distinguish a real extended network from ordinary surname repetition:

* a relationship record connecting John Glasgow alias Smith to the sixteenth-century burgh family;
* parentage evidence linking the Stewart spouses to Minto or another identified Stewart branch;
* parentage evidence linking the Cunningham spouses to Glencairn, Robertland or an Ulster family;
* deeds, wills, correspondence or church records naming kin at both ends of a migration; and
* repeated witnesses, occupations and properties that connect the same identifiable families rather than surnames alone.

== Research priorities ==

# Find the missing conveyances behind the 1527–29 John-to-William transition and the 1551–55 Archibald-to-John boundary sequence.
# Inspect the reported 6 April 1613 parish entry for Robert Glasgow and Jonet Cunningham.
# Verify original parish records for the Alexander–Agnes and James–Jean couples.
# Identify both parents of each spouse before grouping two marriages into one extended family.
# Record occupations, residences, witnesses and property descriptions; treat co-occurrence as association unless the record states kinship.
